learning: Check whether max_error drops below 0.06 m with the agile drivetrain. If it stays near 0.062 m with oscillation low, the limit is controller gain or reaction point, and the next step is a sensor y change or a speed change. If oscillation rises sharply, reduce kp or widen the track.
notes: Keeps the Builder's sensing array unchanged and applies the narrower, lighter, shorter drivetrain. Gains are scaled to the higher yaw response of the 0.09 m track: kp 2.5 (from 3.0) and kd 0.4 (from 0.3). Speed is held at 1.4 to isolate the drivetrain change.
rationale: Iteration 1 showed sensing is no longer the limit: line loss fell from about 1 event per run to 0 with the seven-sensor, 16 mm array, but every run still went off track at max_error about 0.0619 m, and progress fell (oval 0.42 to 0.31). The robot is tracking-limited, so this package changes the drivetrain and keeps the Builder's sensor layout exactly. Track 0.12 to 0.09 m raises yaw per unit of turn command by about 33%, since turn rate is (vL - vR)/wheel_track. To keep the effective steering gain near iteration 1, kp is scaled by 0.09/0.12 (3.0 to 2.25) and rounded up to 2.5 to keep some authority. Lower mass and shorter body reduce yaw inertia, so kd rises from 0.3 to 0.4 to damp the faster heading response and limit oscillation. Sensor weights stay at about 33 times x, as in iteration 1, so the signal scale is unchanged. base_speed stays at 1.4 so this race isolates the drivetrain change; speed remains a possible limit on progress and is the next lever if max_error stays near 0.062 with low oscillation. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m, line_loss near 0, and steering_oscillation no worse than about 0.2 on the oval. This is an estimate, not a measured result.
